scores.concept: Arc-seam rear bridge (flat spine + two stepped shoes)
scores.rationale: FIT 7: the only concept that connects the monitors at mid-height (BRIDGE_Y 160) with real stiffness (120x120x6 PETG channel, 4800 mm2 of tape per side) and the only one that treats the 1800R seam geometry honestly - the 0.79 mm arc fall across a pad and the DT step between two different housings are exactly what a rear bridge on two different chassis needs, and every commercial curved-monitor connector is a rear-adhesive bracket for this reason. What goes wrong: (a) the shoe as sketched cuts the insert holes from the inclined TOP face, which is the VHB face - the tape would cover the insert mouths and the spine screws from the Z=0 side cannot reach them; how_it_attaches says 'inserts on the spine face', the geometry and the plane_gap [0,2] = T(0) - 6.2 assertion say the opposite, so intent and model would agree with each other and both be wrong (PRD Risk 3). Fix: through-holes (tape hides the far end) or blind holes from the bed face asserted by unsupported_area area like the wrx-badge pin ceilings. (b) Bonding is one-shot: the 'spine as placement jig' presses two VHB shoes onto two independently-stood monitors at once; a 0.5 mm error in any of the four caliper inputs exceeds the tape's ~0.3 mm compliance and leaves a shoe bonded on one edge. (c) It does not close or cover the seam at all. (d) It rigidly couples two sprung tilt hinges through tape in peel. PRINT 9: three flat parts on the bed, zero downward faces, no bridges, holes vertical; only the 120x120 PETG plate's corner-lift risk and the terraced 1.13 deg shoe face (cosmetic, under tape). VERIF 8: the best of the three - spine fully Tier 1 by structure (plane_gap [0,1]=6, [1,2]=8; volume window rejects a missing rib at -3840), and the two witness pockets sharing one absolute floor turn the wedge's magnitude AND sign into Tier 1 cylinder_depth readings, which bbox_z and volume cannot see. Deductions: the insert assertions are written to the wrong face; the 1.13 deg incline has |normal_z| = 0.9998 > 0.999 so horizontal_planes() lists it at an arbitrary loc.Z (never index from the top, never assert a plane count on the shoe; it vanishes if a measured taper passes ~2.6 deg); cylinder_depth is z_max - z_min so a bore mouthing on the incline reads its high lip (+0.04 now, +0.10 at 3 deg - widen [6.1,6.3] once tapers are measured). ROBUST 5: parameter separation is clean (spine carries no unknowns, a wrong reading costs one shoe reprint) but only if the error is found BEFORE bonding; no fit-slice step exists, the VHB cannot be repositioned, the toe-in/wedge case is out of scope, a non-planar or flexible rear shell in the pad zone defeats the thickness law, and the B30's rear OSD cluster may sit in the pad zone.

scores.concept: monitor-seam-h-clip (top-corner H-sleeve for the Sceptre B30 / P30 seam)
scores.rationale: FIT 6: closest in spirit to 'a 3D print' - no hardware, no adhesive, lifts off, and a slip-on sleeve indexed on the housing edges genuinely holds front-to-back flush to 0.3 mm and fixes the gap. But it is a top-CORNER clip, not a mid-seam connection, and the bottom cannot be clipped until the B30's rear OSD buttons are mapped, so it covers 60 of 321 mm of seam and resists tilt mismatch only through a 60 mm x 1.6 mm PETG H-section against sprung tilt hinges - it keeps stands that are already set right from drifting; it does not align anything. What goes wrong: the 11.6 mm front web sits 1.6 mm proud on the FRONT of both screens in green PETG; on the edgeless P30 it bears on the glass edge under whatever torsion the stands apply; if the B30 rim is proud the web rides the rim on one side and hovers on the other; 'levels the two top edges in Z' is an overclaim - a sleeve tolerates a height offset, it cannot pull a monitor up (the risks section says so). A non-radial inner end face (a wedge that opens 8-9 mm over 22 mm of depth) kills the 1.6 mm spine outright; the arrangement check catches it, but then the concept is simply gone. PRINT 8: a pure Z-extrusion on a 673 mm2 cap with no downward face - as printable as it gets - except one modelling defect: a 1.0 x 45 deg lead-in on a 1.6 mm front web leaves 0.6 mm at the tip, under the 0.8 min_wall/min_feature BLOCKER, so its own sampled_min_wall [1.5,null] and dfm_violation_count [0,0] assertions would fail as sketched (LEADIN must be <= 0.6 on the front web, or the web thickened to 2.0). 57 mm-tall 1.6 mm PETG walls also need the slicer's minimum layer time respected, which the concept notes. VERIF 6: bbox, plane_gap [0,1]=3 / [1,2]=57, volume floor and unsupported_area are honest Tier 1 claims, and the plane-dedupe reasoning is correct (both slot floors at z=3 collapse to one plane). But the two fit-critical dimensions - SLOT_W_L and SLOT_W_R - are gaps between VERTICAL planes, and MEASURE_KINDS has no measure for that; bbox_y pins only the deeper slot and only if both web thicknesses are trusted. The concept says so plainly and delegates to a physical fit slice; honest, but the part the user cares about is unverifiable by the repository. ROBUST 7: eight caliper readings plus bezel, rim, corner radius and vent surveys is a lot, but the 15 mm fit slice (~3 g) makes every one of them cheap to be wrong about, the failure mode is visible (won't slide on / rattles) rather than bonded, and CLEARANCE 0.3 is sized for the unmeasured PETG_generic hole delta. Loses points because it has exactly one geometry it can be: any wedge seam, rounded end face, or proud-rim-vs-edgeless mismatch beyond 0.3 mm is a different concept, not a parameter edit.

scores.concept: Sceptre B30/P30 VESA arc bridge (V-block + two end brackets + seam cover)
scores.rationale: FIT 4: the only concept that enforces the 1800R continuity by construction (THETA = 11.36 deg in the block) and makes tilt/height/yaw mismatch impossible - real value - but it answers 'a 3D print that connects them in the middle' with a re-mount: both stands removed, a >= 12 kg arm or post bought, 1 m of 2020 cut, T-nuts and M5s sourced, and two 30-inch monitors (11.5 kg total) hung from one printed PETG V-block through four M4 inserts in a 10 mm pad, ~90 mm behind the seam, beside a warm rear cover, forever. As someone who has fitted many dual setups: nobody hangs two curved 30s from a single post via a printed block; a dual arm exists for this, and if either the inserts or the 0.4 mm-slip channels creep, both monitors go together. Also: a 0.4 mm slip on a 20.4 socket over 75 mm is 0.3 deg of pitch play per side, 1.7 mm front-back at a 321 mm housing edge before the M5 clamps take it up; a VESA_DEPTH mismatch between two different chassis (the P30's own published depths disagree by 28 mm) puts the two VESA planes on different circles and the symmetric block cannot fix it; the 96 mm bracket may not fit the neck recess; and the visible full-height seam strip will be green/yellow/purple. PRINT 6: brackets and block are sound (VESA face down, channels open up, counterbores from the top) BUT TEARDROP_DEG 40 was chosen 'under the 45 deg BLOCKER with margin' while specifying PETG, whose rule in profiles/dfm-rules.json is max_overhang_deg 40.0 - the roofs sit exactly on the PETG BLOCKER with zero margin. The 321 x 18 x 1.2 PETG cover strip placed diagonally puts a long thin PETG part with its ends at the coolest corners of the bed: warp/curl risk, and ~8 h of PETG across three parts before the fit-critical dimension has been checked. VERIF 6: the bracket verification is textbook (counterbore + clearance by rank, coaxial_step_radial 1.55, plane_gap 3.5/8/28.4), and verifying THETA by WHERE a witness hole lands (cylinder_diameter at [80, 16.07], tol_xy 0.5 -> 0.36 deg) is a genuinely good Tier 1 trick - provided the hole is modelled in the arm's local frame and rotated with the socket, otherwise it restates the parameter. But CH_W 20.4, the one dimension that decides whether anything fits, is a vertical-plane gap and unverifiable; the M5 clamp holes are horizontal and invisible to the Z-scan; and the overhang assertions test the PLA rule (45) on a PETG part, so dfm_violation_count PETG_generic == 0 is on a knife edge (ang > 40.0). ROBUST 4: ten must-measure items, several about hardware that does not yet exist (the arm head, the extrusion, the X-plate's hole type/thickness/proudness, boss depth for M4x14 bottoming), plus VESA depth per side, keep-outs, border widths and rim steps. Per-side VESA_DEPTH and THETA are parametrised, and THETA = 0 gives a flat butt joint, but a large VESA mismatch is a new asymmetric block, and once the stands are off there is no cheap way back.

winner: Arc-seam rear bridge (flat spine + two stepped shoes) - wins on verifiability (the only concept whose fit-critical geometry, including the wedge's sign, is Tier 1 in-repo) and on actually connecting the monitors at mid-height with adequate stiffness, while treating the 1800R seam honestly. Two conditions before intent.json is written: (1) fix the shoe so the insert holes open toward the spine (Z=0 face), not the VHB face - through-holes or bed-face blind holes asserted by unsupported_area - and rewrite the plane_gap/cylinder_depth assertions to the corrected side; (2) graft the H-clip's print-first fit check: print ONE shoe and dry-fit it to its rear cover with a rule and feeler before any VHB is peeled, so the four caliper numbers are proven on the part rather than discovered by a bond that cannot be undone.
graft_from_others: From the H-clip: the cheap fit-slice-before-commitment step. For the bridge that means printing one shoe (~45 g) and dry-fitting it to its own rear cover with a steel rule and feeler - reading the residual gap at the pad's inner and outer edges - before any VHB is applied. The bridge's failure mode is a bond that cannot be repositioned; the H-clip's discipline is that the irreversible step never happens on an unproven number.

From the H-clip: the no-caliper arrangement check as the FIRST question to the user - look down the seam from above; an even gap front-to-back means one continuous arc and the bridge applies, a wedge means a hinge and none of these three concepts do. Ask it before asking for any of the four caliper readings.

From the VESA bridge: the honest framing of the arrangement binary. 'Each monitor centred on the viewer' is geometrically impossible for two side-by-side panels; the real alternative to the continuous arc is a flat butt joint (THETA = 0). Put that binary to the user instead of the 'toed-in at 0.7 m' strawman, whose wedge angle the two other concepts do not even agree on (38 vs 27 deg).

From the VESA bridge: the full-height front seam cover - a 1.2 mm T-strip with a 2.4 mm keel located in the seam gap, printed diagonally - as an optional second print. The bridge supplies the connection; the strip supplies the 'close the seam' half of the interpretation the bridge leaves untouched. Keep it separate so it can be omitted if the green filament on the front is unwanted, and note that the bridge's SEAM_GAP 2.0 must be raised to ~3.0 for the keel.

From the VESA bridge: verifying an angle by hole POSITION at Tier 1 (cylinder_diameter at [x, y] with tol_xy 0.5 -> the assertion FAILS 'absent' if the angle is wrong). The bridge's shoes already pin the wedge through witness depths, but if a seam-angle variant is ever needed this is the pattern for making a rotation Tier 1 without any angle measure kind.

From the H-clip: its explicit plane-set bookkeeping ('the two floors sit at the same z so they dedupe to one plane; a step would add a third'). Apply the same audit to the shoe, where the 1.13 deg incline registers as a horizontal plane (|normal_z| 0.9998 > 0.999) at an arbitrary z and drops out past ~2.6 deg - so index planes from the bottom only and never assert a plane count on the shoe.

From the H-clip: removability as a design value. The bridge's spine already unbolts; consider making the VHB-bonded piece a thin flat base plate with the stepped/wedged shoe screwed to it, so a wrong wedge is a reprint rather than a cut-and-clean of the tape.

scores.concept: Arc-seam rear bridge (flat spine + two stepped shoes)
scores.rationale: FIT 7: acts 16-56 mm from the seam and references the GLASS (T_EDGE is glass-to-rear, not rim-to-rear), so the flush step DT is a caliper number and the arc is held by shoes wedged tangent at +/-36 mm (1.13 deg, consistent with ARC_RISE 0.79 over 40) -- the tightest seam control of the three, stands stay, spine unbolts. Docked for: nothing closes the 2 mm seam; VHB is one-shot with no post-bond trim; two sprung tilt stands are locked through a peel-loaded bond; the survey checks the housing only at y = 160 while the pad is 120 mm tall on a cover that thickens toward mid-height, so a Y-taper under the pad is unasked and 1.1 mm foam absorbs only ~0.3. Geometry inconsistency to fix before intent.json: the text puts the M3 inserts on the spine face (screws from behind through the 6 mm plate) but cuts the O4.0 blind holes from the inclined BONDING face with floors at 3.2/5.2 mm above the bed -- under the tape, unreachable by the screws (the plane_gap [0,2] assertion confirms the floors are above the bed). Make them O4.0 through-holes: a blind hole from the Z=0 face would put two 12.6 mm2 ceilings into unsupported_area and fail the [0,1] window (the wrx-badge precedent asserts ceilings by area), whereas a through-hole has no ceiling, the tape covers the exit, and cylinder_depth at (0,+/-40) becomes a third independent read of T(0). PRINTABILITY 9: three bed-down parts, no downward face but the plate face, terraces on a 1.1 deg top are cosmetic and under tape; the 120x120x6 PETG plate is the only warp candidate and the ribs help. VERIFIABILITY 9: checked against features.py -- the inclined top fails _mesh_planes' flat test (tri Z range < 1e-6) so it inserts no phantom plane and the [0,1]/[0,2] indices hold; the O3 pockets are found by ring-count transitions bisected to 0.002 mm; the pocket run ends at the mouth's low edge (~9.03 vs 9.06 at centre), inside the stated [7.0,7.15]; the shared-floor witness depths are the only Tier 1 read of the wedge's SIGN, and per-shoe bbox_z reads DT. Only the incline-as-angle and the assembled flushness are outside the ruler, and both are declared. ROBUSTNESS 7: every unknown is quarantined in two ~50 g shoes and the spine carries none; step/wedge formulas hold for either sign; nothing is a press fit; a wrong number costs one small reprint. Weak spots: one-shot bond, no Y-direction survey, hand placement of the jigged assembly, toed-in arrangement is fatal (stated).

scores.concept: monitor-seam-h-clip (top-corner H-sleeve for the Sceptre B30 / P30 seam)
scores.rationale: FIT 5: a 60 mm keeper at one corner of a 320 mm seam; the front web covers 60/320 of it and the bottom is unconstrained. Where it acts it is the most direct of the three (0.3 mm slip at the edge itself, no adhesive, no hardware, lifts off). But it references the front RIM, not the glass: the B30 rim is proud and the P30 is edgeless, so 'flush rims' means the glass steps by the rim height, and RIM_STEP is a check rather than geometry. The rear web bears 0-12 mm inboard -- exactly the zone Concept 1 places a rearward facet (placeholder 12) -- and the 1.6 mm spine assumes the inner end faces are radial and parallel; if they are perpendicular to each chord the gap opens ~8 mm over 22 mm of depth and the sleeve is the wrong concept. A 60 mm lever on 1.6 mm PETG webs will not hold a tilt mismatch; PETG creeps. PRINTABILITY 9: 11 g, cap-down, every face a Z-extrusion, lead-ins face up, chamfers correctly kept off the bed edge; 1.6 mm walls 57 mm tall are a slicer minimum-layer-time matter, not a DFM one. VERIFIABILITY 5: the four dimensions that make the part work (SLOT_W_L, SLOT_W_R, two REAR_TAPER planes) are vertical-plane gaps the ruler cannot measure; bbox_y pins only the deeper slot, and with equal placeholders it pins neither. Cap thickness, web height, volume floor and overhang 0 are real Tier 1 claims but are not the function; the 15 mm fit slice is a physical test outside the loop. ROBUSTNESS 4: the tallest assumption stack -- parallel-sided seam, edge depth constant within 0.3 over 60 mm, plain cover in the first 12 mm, flat top edge with no vent within 13 mm, small corner radius, equal rim heights, stand heights matched under 1 mm, equal tilts -- and several failures (V-shaped seam, corner radius, rim step) are geometry changes rather than parameter edits. The 3 g fit slice in 15 minutes is the mitigation, and it is a good one.

scores.concept: Sceptre B30/P30 VESA arc bridge (V-block + two end brackets + seam cover)
scores.rationale: FIT 5: the only concept that removes tilt mismatch by construction, covers the whole seam, lets the gap be set by sliding the bars, and makes 1800R drive real geometry (THETA 11.36 deg). But it is a mounting system, not a connector: both stands come off; it needs 2020 extrusion, T-nuts, eight M5s and a >=12 kg arm; and 11.5 kg hangs on four M4 heat-set inserts in a 10 mm PETG pad beside warm electronics (creep, permanent load). Seam flush is set 90 mm behind the seam and 376 mm from each VESA with no trim: 0.4 mm bar clearance over a 75 mm socket (0.3 deg) and the 0.36 deg witness tolerance each project to ~2 mm of front-back step at the seam edge; each 414 mm 2020 half deflects ~1.8 mm under a 5 kg monitor (PL^3/3EI). No must-measure for the VESA's vertical position on two different chassis, so a height step at the seam is unguarded. PRINTABILITY 6: brackets and block are chunky and bed-down, but TEARDROP_DEG 40 is justified as 'under the 45 deg BLOCKER' while the material is PETG_generic whose BLOCKER is 40; dfm._judge is `measured > threshold`, and float32 STL vertices put the recomputed roof normal on either side of 40.0000 deg, so `dfm_violation_count == 0` is a coin flip -- drop the roof to 35 deg. The 321x18x1.2 PETG strip on the diagonal is a corner-lift candidate and floppy off the plate; ~8 h of PETG committed on an unmeasured hole delta. VERIFIABILITY 7: bracket assertions are exactly right (counterbore coaxial_step_radial 1.55, plane gaps 3.5/8/28.4) and verifying THETA by WHERE a witness hole is rather than what size it is is the best trick in the three concepts. But CH_W 20.4 -- the dimension all three structural prints depend on -- is a vertical-plane gap and unverifiable (acknowledged), and the M5 holes are horizontal and unseen by the Z-scan. ROBUSTNESS 4: ten must-measures including bought hardware and a stand removal the user has not agreed to; the P30's published depth spans 81-109 so VESA_DEPTH may differ between monitors by more than the symmetric block can absorb; X-plate proud/recessed and boss depth decide whether the bracket rocks or the M4x14 bottoms while feeling tight; tolerances amplify through 350 mm lever arms with no adjustment beyond sliding the bars.

winner: Arc-seam rear bridge (flat spine + two stepped shoes)
graft_from_others: From the VESA bridge: a full-height seam cover strip (T-section on the borders, keel into the gap, underside RIM_STEP_L/R steps) so the bridge also closes the 2 mm seam; this pulls BORDER and RIM_STEP onto the must-measure list. A keel in a 2 mm gap is 1.4 mm (above min_wall 0.8 but flimsy) -- consider SEAM_GAP 3.

From the H-clip: measure the edge depth at more than one height. For the bridge, T_EDGE at 100, 160 and 220 mm (top, centre, bottom of the 120 mm pad) so a Y-taper of the housing under the pad is a number, not an assumption; the shoe then gets a second wedge axis or PAD_H shrinks.

From the H-clip: the fit-slice discipline. Print the two shoes (or a 10 mm slice of each) first and dry-fit them on the backs with a straightedge before printing the spine and before any tape touches a monitor.

From the VESA bridge: adjustability. Slot the spine's four holes +/-2 mm along X so the seam gap can be trimmed before final tightening, and print a 0.2/0.4 mm shim pack for between shoe and spine so a wrong DT is a shim, not cut tape and a reprint.

From the VESA bridge: through-hole heat-set inserts ('the through hole means an over-long screw cannot bottom'). This also resolves the bridge's insert-face inconsistency (inserts must be in the Z=0 spine face), keeps unsupported_area at 0, and makes cylinder_depth at (0,+/-40) a third independent read of T(0).

From the H-clip: the no-caliper look-down-the-seam check as the FIRST must-measure. A wedge-shaped gap reveals either a toed-in arrangement or non-radial end faces; both are fatal to a flat spine referenced to the rear, and neither is caught by the bridge's verbal 'confirm the arrangement'.

From the VESA bridge: a creep watch -- re-check the seam with a rule at three heights after a week; the bridge holds a sustained tilt torque in PETG next to a warm housing and its witness depths say nothing about creep.

scores.concept: Arc-seam rear bridge (flat spine + two stepped shoes)
scores.rationale: FIT 7. The one design that understands the actual geometry of the seam: front glass on one 1800R circle, rear surfaces on 1800+t, so a rear-referenced bridge must carry a thickness step DT = T_EDGE_R - T_EDGE_L plus a 0.79 mm wedge per pad, and it derives both from the four caliper numbers by formula with the sign preserved. Nothing enters the seam, so it is immune to the end-face-angle trap that kills the other two (an end face cut square to the chord rather than radial opens an 11 mm rear wedge at 22.7 deg on the shared arc). What it does NOT do: cover or close the seam (the user asked to 'connect in the middle'; a visible 2 mm gap remains), constrain the top/bottom of the seam except through spine torsion (my estimate for a 6 mm plate with two 8 mm open ribs over the 32 mm free span is ~0.27 deg/N.m, the same order as their 0.17; a 0.3 deg tilt mismatch is 0.8 mm at the top edge), or survive a later single-stand tilt (VHB in peel). Semi-permanent tape on an electronics housing, one-shot placement. B30 OSD cluster at the inner-lower rear corner may sit in the pad zone; survey decides. PRINT 9. Three flat parts, every face vertical or upward, no bridges, no supports, thinnest wall 1.5 mm, smallest hole 3.0; the 1.1 deg incline prints as ~10 mm terraces under tape. Only the 120x120 PETG plate's first-layer adhesion is worth a brim decision. VERIFIABILITY 7 -- strong intent, but the shoe assertions as written fail their own baseline on the mesh path, which is the path the mutation suite scores. plane_transitions samples every 0.5 mm and bisects to ONE transition per interval, and a hole's z_max is the slab boundary, not the local surface. Right shoe: samples at z=9.0 and 9.5 straddle three ring-count changes (inner witness mouth 9.03, insert mouths ~9.36, outer witness ~9.70); only 9.03 is found. Result: insert depth reads 9.03-3.195 = 5.84 against the asserted [6.1,6.3] -> baseline FAIL; outer witness reads 9.79-2.0 = 7.79 against [7.65,7.8] -> passes by 0.01. The reversed-wedge case IS caught (inner 7.79, outer 7.03, both outside their windows) but for a structural reason, not the one claimed. Second trap: on the BREP path horizontal_planes() admits |normal_z|>0.999 (2.56 deg) so the 1.13 deg top IS a 'horizontal plane' on STEP at OCCT's arbitrary plane-location z, and is NOT one on STL (flat-triangle filter); cross_check compares cylinder radii only, so this divergence is silent -- harmless at indices 0-2, fatal if any assertion ever indexes the top. Fix is cheap: spot-face every hole mouth on the incline with a horizontal counterbore a fixed depth below the local surface (also correct practice under a heat-set flange), then choose depths so every distinct horizontal plane sits >= 0.5 mm from its neighbours and in a different 0.5 mm scan window; the witness depths then read the local height exactly and the sign claim becomes real. The spine is fully Tier 1 as written (plane_gap 6/8, four 3.4 holes by count and position, depth 6.0, volume window that drops a rib). ROBUSTNESS 6. Fewest unknowns (four caliper numbers + a keep-out survey), all absorbed by formula in either sign, invariant spine. But VHB cannot be repositioned, a non-planar or textured rear cover defeats the foam's 0.3 mm budget, PETG needs primer for VHB, and a toe-in arrangement or a raised rear cover inside 16-56 mm ends the concept. Nothing here is cheap to iterate physically.

scores.concept: monitor-seam-h-clip (top-corner H-sleeve for the Sceptre B30 / P30 seam)
scores.rationale: FIT 5. A 60 mm slip-on at one corner registers front-back flush (0.3 mm), seam gap and top-edge height, and is the only concept the user can fit and remove in seconds with no hardware or adhesive. But it is a seam clip, not a connector: the bottom of the seam is unconstrained (deferred for the B30 OSD buttons), so the two bases can still splay in X and any tilt mismatch is resisted by 1.6-2.4 mm PETG webs on a 60 mm lever, loaded across layer lines at the root. It covers 60 mm of a 321 mm seam with an 11.6 mm strip 1.6 mm proud of the glass, in green/yellow/purple against black bezels, right where the user looks. The 5 mm front reach bears on the P30's edgeless glass border, and the spine needs the two inner side faces parallel: on a shared arc that is only true if the end faces are radial; if either housing's end face is cut square to its chord the seam is a wedge and the spine cannot enter -- their arrangement check would misread that as toe-in. Edge depth almost certainly varies over the top 60 mm of a curved housing; a 0.3 mm slip absorbs 0.3 mm of that and no more. PRINT 7. Clean against dfm-rules (no overhang, no bridge, 673 mm2 footprint, aspect 2.3), cap-down with the lead-in chamfers facing up is the right call, and refusing a bed-side chamfer for PETG's 40 deg rule is correct. Practically: three 57 mm tall walls of 4-6 beads in PETG with very short layer times -- minimum layer time and stringing between webs will decide the part, and the front web is the weakest orientation for its load. VERIFIABILITY 5. Everything asserted is genuinely Tier 1 on both paths (planes at 0, 3, 60 -> plane_gap 3 and 57; bbox; a volume floor that drops a web; unsupported_area 0 at 40 deg), and the concept is honest that the fit-critical dimensions -- both slot widths, the rear-web step and both tapers -- are vertical-plane gaps the ruler cannot see. But that honesty leaves the intent verifying only the envelope: bbox_y pins the SUM front web + deeper slot + rear web, so a 2.6 mm front web with a 21.3 slot passes identically. The 15 mm fit slice is the real verification and it is physical, not intent.json. ROBUSTNESS 5. Eight caliper readings, and the design dies on any of: edge taper along Z over 0.3 mm, a top-inner corner radius over ~2 mm, a vent slot inside 13 mm, a bezel under 6 mm, or non-parallel end faces. What saves it is cost: a failed guess is 3 g of PETG and nothing is glued, so iteration is cheap and reversible -- the best failure mode of the three.

scores.concept: Sceptre B30/P30 VESA arc bridge (V-block + two end brackets + seam cover)
scores.rationale: FIT 4. Geometrically the most complete answer -- angle fixed by construction, one tilt for both, full-height seam cover -- and the least responsive to the ask: 'a 3D print that connects the two monitors in the middle' becomes remove both stands, buy a >=12 kg desk arm, 2020 extrusion, T-nuts and M5 hardware, and hang ~11.5 kg of monitor from four M4 inserts in PETG and two 3.5 mm webs, permanently loaded beside warm electronics. Worse, the centre block as drawn does not assemble: the arc bends about a vertical axis, so the two tangent bars meet in a V in the HORIZONTAL plane (the plane containing the front-back direction). The block is printed rear pad down with sockets 'open toward the monitors', which makes print Z the front-back axis -- and the arms are then rotated in the print XY plane ('vertical walls at +/-11.36 deg in plan', 'floors coplanar at Z=10', witness at (80, 16.07)). That is a V in the screen-parallel plane, where the bars are neither tangent to the arc nor horizontal, and the brackets' horizontal channels cannot take them. The only reading that makes the geometry right has the pad facing DOWN onto a post top, which is not what a desk arm's tilting VESA head offers and contradicts 'rear pad'. One of {coplanar floors, witness position, rearward pad} must give. PRINT 5. The bracket is textbook (VESA face down, counterbores open up, no bridges). But the teardrop roofs are drawn at exactly 40 deg while specifying PETG, whose max_overhang_deg BLOCKER is 40.0 and dfm.py's test is 'measured > threshold' -- one floating-point ulp of face-normal arithmetic from a BLOCKER, and the text cites 'under the 45 deg BLOCKER', the PLA rule. Draw them at 38. A 170 mm block plus two 96x96x28 brackets is many hours of PETG, and a 321x18x1.2 strip laid diagonally is the classic first-layer lift. VERIFIABILITY 5. The bracket intent is the bearing-holder pattern done properly: counterbore vs clearance by rank at each corner, coaxial_step_radial 1.55, plane_gap 3.5/8/28.4, feature counts, a real check that head_h 4.0 fits in the 4.5 counterbore. Verifying THETA by the POSITION of a witness hole (tol_xy 0.5 over 80 mm = 0.36 deg, absent -> FAIL) is the best single ruler idea across all three concepts. But it verifies the model's own rotation in whatever plane the model used, and the model uses the wrong one -- intent and geometry agreeing with each other while both are wrong is PRD Risk 3 exactly. The fit-critical channel width (20.4) is a vertical gap, unverifiable, acknowledged, coupon proposed. The seam cover's keel via plane_gap is fine. ROBUSTNESS 3.
